title: Affine Sets: Geometry Without An Origin
notes: Open by removing the origin from the story. A linear subspace is tied to zero, while an affine set keeps only the direction rules. Ask students to read every object as a translate of a direction space, then preview the computational tests that will certify membership, dimension, and projection.

title: Affine Versus Linear
notes: Use the parallel lines to separate two closure rules. Linear structure lets every scalar multiple remain in the set, so zero is unavoidable. Affine structure only protects combinations whose coefficients add to one, which is why the translated line is legal even though the drawn origin is not on it.

title: Affine Combinations
notes: The coefficient-sum condition is the entire hinge of the section. Nonnegative coefficients give convex combinations, but affine combinations permit negative weights and can move beyond the segment or triangle. Emphasize that the sum equal to one preserves location relative to the chosen points, independent of the coordinate origin.

title: Lines, Flats, And Translates
notes: Introduce flats as shifted subspaces, not as new mysterious objects. A point a anchors the set, while the direction space L supplies all allowed displacements. Lines, planes, and hyperplanes differ by the dimension of L or by the number of independent equations used to describe the translate.

title: Affine Hull As Smallest Flat
notes: Frame the affine hull as a closure operation with a concrete recipe. Pick one base point, subtract it from the remaining points, span those differences, and shift the resulting linear subspace back by the base point. The rank ledger in the slide-local asset records exactly what dimension this produces.

title: Solving Membership By Linear Equations
notes: Membership is not a matter of visual guesswork. After choosing a base point, solve the linear system whose columns are differences from that base. A zero residual gives coefficients for an affine combination; a nonzero normal-equation residual is a certificate that the candidate sits outside the flat.

title: Affine Independence
notes: Affine independence is linear independence after translation. The test ignores absolute position by anchoring at p0 and asking whether the difference vectors are linearly independent. Three noncollinear points in space pass the rank two test, while adding a fourth point in their plane creates dependence.

title: Dimension From Rank
notes: Connect the geometric word dimension to an auditable matrix rank. A point has affine dimension zero, a line has dimension one, a plane has dimension two, and so on. The important habit is to compute rank from differences, because raw point coordinates would incorrectly remember the arbitrary origin.

title: Relative Coordinates / Barycentric View
notes: Barycentric coordinates make affine position portable. The same coefficients reconstruct the point after any translation of the whole configuration, because the coefficients sum to one. This is also the clean way to tell convex and affine stories apart: convex insists on nonnegative weights, affine does not.

title: Intersections Of Affine Sets
notes: The intersection of affine sets stays affine because the combined equation system is still linear after translation. Demonstrate the practical test: stack the equations, check consistency, and read the dimension from the nullity of the stacked direction constraints. Empty intersections are the one failure case.

title: Projection To The Affine Hull
notes: Projection adds an optimization certificate to the membership picture. The closest point in the affine hull leaves a residual perpendicular to every direction vector in L. The slide-local check records two dot products equal to zero, so the picture is backed by the same linear algebra used for membership.

title: Failure Modes: Convex Is Not Affine
notes: Use this as a diagnostic slide. A segment or filled triangle is convex because averages stay inside, but it is not affine because affine coefficients with a negative entry escape the set. Conversely, a full affine line is affine but usually not bounded or region-like. Closure rules decide the name.

title: Computational Checklist
notes: Turn the lecture into a repeatable workflow. Normalize the data by choosing a base point, form the difference matrix, compute rank, solve membership, inspect residuals, test independence, and verify projection orthogonality when needed. These checks are deliberately small enough to run in a notebook or by hand.

title: Recap / Inspection Prompt
notes: Close by asking students to produce certificates rather than definitions. Given points and a candidate x, they should identify the affine hull, compute its dimension, find coefficients that sum to one or a residual proving failure, and explain how translating the origin would leave the answer unchanged.
